title: p-Block Elements: Group 13 & 14 (Electronic Configurations, Oxidation States, & Anomalous Properties)
syllabus: Group 13 elements (Boron family: B, Al, Ga, In, Tl): General characteristics, electronic configurations, atomic and ionic radii, ionization enthalpies, and electronegativity; Inert pair effect and stability of +1 vs +3 oxidation states; Anomalous properties and diagonal relationship of boron with silicon; Electron-deficient nature, Lewis acidity of boron trihalides, structure and 3c-2e bonding in diborane (B2H6); Borax bead test, orthoboric acid (H3BO3) and its Lewis acidic behavior; Amphoteric character of Al and Ga oxides/hydroxides; Group 14 elements (Carbon family: C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb): General trends, catenation, multiple bonding (pπ-pπ vs pπ-dπ), allotropes of carbon (diamond, graphite, fullerenes, graphene); Inert pair effect and relative stabilities of +2 vs +4 oxidation states (Sn and Pb redox behavior); Anomalous behavior of carbon; Oxides of carbon (CO, CO2), silicates and silicones structures and classifications

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The correct order of relative Lewis acid strength among boron trihalides is:
questions.solution:
In boron trihalides ($\text{BX}_3$), the central boron atom has an incomplete octet with a vacant unhybridized $2p$ orbital, allowing back-donation of electron density from filled $p$-orbitals of the halogen through $p\pi-p\pi$ back-bonding:
1. In $\text{BF}_3$, there is effective $2p\pi(\text{B})-2p\pi(\text{F})$ overlap due to identical orbital size and low energy gap, substantially mitigating the electron deficiency of boron.
2. In $\text{BCl}_3$, $\text{BBr}_3$, and $\text{BI}_3$, the halogens use $3p$, $4p$, and $5p$ orbitals respectively. The mismatch in orbital size with boron's compact $2p$ orbital sharply decreases the extent of back-donation.
3. Because back-bonding is weakest in $\text{BI}_3$ and strongest in $\text{BF}_3$, the tendency of boron to accept an external electron pair (Lewis acidity) follows the order:
$$\text{BF}_3 < \text{BCl}_3 < \text{BBr}_3 < \text{BI}_3$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The relative stabilities of $+1$ and $+3$ oxidation states for Group 13 elements follow which of the following trends down the group?
options: Stability of $+1$ state increases, while $+3$ state decreases
Stability of $+3$ state increases, while $+1$ state decreases
Stability of both $+1$ and $+3$ states increases
Stability of both $+1$ and $+3$ states decreases
questions.solution:
Due to the **inert pair effect**, the reluctance of the outermost valence $ns^2$ electron pair to participate in chemical bonding increases as we descend Group 13 (as intervening $d$ and $f$ electrons provide poor shielding of nuclear charge).
Consequently:
- The group oxidation state ($+3$) becomes progressively less stable down the group: $\text{B}^{3+} > \text{Al}^{3+} > \text{Ga}^{3+} > \text{In}^{3+} > \text{Tl}^{3+}$.
- The lower oxidation state ($+1$) becomes progressively more stable: $\text{B}^+ < \text{Al}^+ < \text{Ga}^+ < \text{In}^+ < \text{Tl}^+$.
Thus, for thallium ($\text{Tl}$), the $+1$ oxidation state is far more stable than $+3$, making $\text{Tl}^{3+}$ a powerful oxidizing agent.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The atomic radius of gallium ($\text{Ga}$) is slightly smaller than that of aluminum ($\text{Al}$). This anomalous trend is primarily attributed to:
options: Ineffective shielding of the nuclear charge by poor screening $3d$-electrons in gallium
Greater screening effect of $3p$-electrons in aluminum
questions.solution:
Electronic configurations:
- $\text{Al}: [\text{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^1$
- $\text{Ga}: [\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^1$
Between aluminum and gallium, there are ten transition elements where the $3d$ subshell is progressively filled.
Because $d$-orbitals are diffuse in shape, they screen the outer valence $4s$ and $4p$ electrons very poorly from the increased nuclear charge ($10$ additional protons).
This causes an increase in effective nuclear charge ($Z_{\text{eff}}$) for gallium, pulling the valence electrons inward.
Consequently, the atomic radius of gallium ($135\text{ pm}$) is slightly less than that of aluminum ($143\text{ pm}$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In the diborane molecule ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$), which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: All six $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bonds are identical in bond length and bond strength
It contains four terminal $2\text{c}-2\text{e}^-$ $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bonds and two bridging $3\text{c}-2\text{e}^-$ $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ bonds
Both boron atoms are in $sp^3$ hybridization
The four terminal hydrogen atoms and the two boron atoms lie in the same plane
questions.solution:
In diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$):
1. The two boron atoms and the four terminal hydrogen atoms lie in one plane.
2. The four terminal $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bonds are conventional two-center two-electron ($2\text{c}-2\text{e}^-$) covalent bonds ($119\text{ pm}$).
3. The two bridge hydrogen atoms lie above and below this plane, forming two three-center two-electron ($3\text{c}-2\text{e}^-$) banana bonds ($	ext{B}-	ext{H}-	ext{B}$, $133\text{ pm}$).
4. Both boron atoms are $sp^3$ hybridized.
Because the bridge bonds are longer and weaker than the terminal bonds, Statement A is incorrect.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Solid $\text{PbO}_2$ reacts with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ to liberate oxygen gas, whereas $\text{SnO}_2$ does not act as an oxidizing agent. This observation demonstrates that:
options: $\text{Pb}^{4+}$ is an oxidizing agent due to the inert pair effect, while $\text{Sn}^{4+}$ is stable
$\text{PbO}_2$ is a basic oxide while $\text{SnO}_2$ is amphoteric
questions.solution:
In Group 14, due to the inert pair effect:
- For tin ($\text{Sn}$), the $+4$ oxidation state is more stable than $+2$. Therefore, $\text{Sn}^{2+}$ acts as a reducing agent (oxidizing readily to $\text{Sn}^{4+}$).
- For lead ($\text{Pb}$), the $+2$ oxidation state is far more stable than $+4$. Hence, $\text{Pb}^{4+}$ (in $\text{PbO}_2$) readily accepts electrons to reduce to $\text{Pb}^{2+}$, making it a powerful oxidizing agent:
$$2\text{PbO}_2 + 4\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{Pb(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2 \uparrow$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Orthoboric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3$) behaves as a monobasic acid in aqueous solution because:
options: It acts as a Lewis acid by accepting an electron pair from a water molecule's $\text{OH}^-$, releasing a proton
It donates one of its ionizable protons directly from an internal $-\text{OH}$ group
It forms a stable dibasic adduct with hydronium ions
It undergoes disproportionation into metaboric acid and boric oxide
questions.solution:
Orthoboric acid ($\text{B(OH)}_3$) is not a typical Brønsted-Lowry proton donor. Boron has only six valence electrons and an incomplete octet (Lewis acid).
In aqueous solution, it accepts a pair of electrons from the oxygen of a water molecule (acting as a Lewis acid), thereby releasing a hydronium ion:
$$\text{B(OH)}_3(aq) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons [\text{B(OH)}_4]^-(aq) + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+(aq) \quad (pK_a \approx 9.25)$$
Hence, it behaves as a weak monobasic Lewis acid.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Catenation tendency among Group 14 elements follows which of the following orders?
questions.solution:
Catenation (the ability of an element to form covalent bonds with atoms of the same kind to form long chains or rings) depends primarily on the element-element bond dissociation enthalpy:
- $\text{C}-\text{C}$: $348\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{Si}-\text{Si}$: $297\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{Ge}-\text{Ge}$: $260\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{Sn}-\text{Sn}$: $240\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{Pb}-\text{Pb}$: negligible
Because the carbon-carbon single bond is exceptionally strong due to small atomic size and effective overlap, catenation is maximal in carbon and decreases sharply down the group:
$$\text{C} \gg \text{Si} > \text{Ge} \approx \text{Sn} > \text{Pb}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following statements about fullerenes (such as $\text{C}_{60}$) is TRUE?
options: $\text{C}_{60}$ contains $20$ six-membered rings and $12$ five-membered rings
$\text{C}_{60}$ contains $12$ six-membered rings and $20$ five-membered rings
All carbon atoms in fullerenes are $sp^3$ hybridized
Five-membered rings can be fused to other five-membered rings
questions.solution:
Buckminsterfullerene ($\text{C}_{60}$) has a soccer-ball cage structure (truncated icosahedron):
1. It consists of $20$ six-membered hexagonal rings and $12$ five-membered pentagonal rings (Euler's polyhedral theorem requires exactly 12 pentagons to close a trivalent cage).
2. Six-membered rings can be fused to both other six-membered rings and five-membered rings.
3. Five-membered rings are isolated and fused ONLY to six-membered rings (Isolated Pentagon Rule).
4. All carbon atoms are $sp^2$ hybridized with slight pyramidalization.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) and silicon tetrachloride ($\text{SiCl}_4$) are treated with water, which of the following behaviors is observed?
options: $\text{SiCl}_4$ undergoes rapid hydrolysis, whereas $\text{CCl}_4$ is completely inert towards hydrolysis
$\text{CCl}_4$ undergoes rapid hydrolysis, while $\text{SiCl}_4$ does not hydrolyze
Neither compound undergoes hydrolysis under standard conditions
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of halides occurs by nucleophilic attack of a water molecule lone pair on the central atom:
1. In $\text{CCl}_4$, carbon belongs to Period 2 and has only $2s$ and $2p$ valence orbitals. Because it lacks low-lying vacant $d$-orbitals, it cannot expand its coordination number beyond four to accept an incoming lone pair from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Furthermore, carbon is sterically shielded by four chlorine atoms. Thus, $\text{CCl}_4$ is inert to hydrolysis.
2. In $\text{SiCl}_4$, silicon belongs to Period 3 and possesses vacant $3d$-orbitals. Silicon readily expands its coordination sphere to coordinate with water (forming an unstable pentacoordinate intermediate $[\text{SiCl}_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})]$), hydrolyzing completely to silicic acid ($\text{H}_4\text{SiO}_4$ or $\text{SiO}_2 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) and $\text{HCl}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The borax bead test with copper sulfate in an oxidizing flame produces a bead with which of the following colors in the cold?
questions.solution:
In the borax bead test:
1. On heating, borax loses its water of crystallization and swells, then melts to form a clear transparent vitreous bead composed of sodium metaborate and boric anhydride:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{NaBO}_2 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3$$
2. When reacted with copper sulfate in an oxidizing flame, cupric metaborate is formed:
$$\text{CuO} + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$$
Cupric metaborate ($\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$) gives a characteristic dark **blue** bead in the cold (and green when hot).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The basic structural building unit of all silicate minerals is:
questions.solution:
The fundamental building block of all naturally occurring and synthetic silicates is the discrete $[\text{SiO}_4]^{4-}$ tetrahedral unit.
In this unit, the central silicon atom is $sp^3$ hybridized and covalently bonded to four oxygen atoms located at the corners of a regular tetrahedron.
Different classes of silicates (ortho-, pyro-, cyclic, chain, sheet, and three-dimensional framework silicates) arise from sharing $0, 1, 2, 3,$ or $4$ corner oxygen atoms between adjacent $[\text{SiO}_4]^{4-}$ tetrahedra.

questions.question: Which of the following elements in Group 13 forms a hydride that is an electron-precise ionic solid at room temperature?
questions.solution:
Group 13 elements possess three valence electrons ($ns^2 np^1$).
When they form binary covalent hydrides ($MH_3$), they have only six valence electrons surrounding the central metal atom, making them inherently electron-deficient (such as the bridged polymers in $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$ or polymeric $(\text{AlH}_3)_n$).
None of the Group 13 hydrides are electron-precise or form simple ionic salt-like hydrides under standard conditions (ionic hydrides are characteristic of alkali and alkaline earth metals in the s-block).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The reaction of dimethyldichlorosilane, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{SiCl}_2$, with water followed by condensation polymerization yields:
questions.solution:
1. Hydrolysis of dimethyldichlorosilane replaces the chlorine atoms with hydroxyl groups:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{SiCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{Si(OH)}_2 + 2\text{HCl}$$
2. The resulting dimethylsilanediol possesses two reactive $-\text{OH}$ groups. Intermolecular dehydration condensation between terminal silanol groups leads to propagation along a single direction:
$$\dots-\text{O}-\text{Si}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{O}-\text{Si}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{O}-\dots$$
This produces a **linear chain silicone polymer** (or cyclic oligomers like $(\text{Me}_2\text{SiO})_n$). Cross-linked polymers require trichlorosilanes ($\text{RSiCl}_3$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In graphite, the hybridization of each carbon atom and the electrical conductivity along the hexagonal sheets are due to:
options: $sp^2$, delocalized $\pi$-electrons mobile within the hexagonal planes
$sp^2$, presence of free interstitial metal cations
questions.solution:
In graphite:
1. Each carbon atom is $sp^2$ hybridized and forms three planar $\sigma$ bonds with adjacent carbon atoms at $120^\circ$, creating two-dimensional hexagonal layers (graphene sheets).
2. The fourth valence electron of each carbon occupies an unhybridized $2p_z$ orbital oriented perpendicular to the layer.
3. These $p$-orbitals overlap extensively to produce a continuous delocalized $\pi$-electron cloud extending across the entire sheet.
4. Under an applied electric potential, these delocalized electrons move freely within the parallel planes, imparting high electrical and thermal conductivity along the sheets.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Why does boron form only $\text{BF}_4^-$ and cannot form $\text{BF}_6^{3-}$, whereas aluminum readily forms $\text{AlF}_6^{3-}$?
options: Boron has no vacant $d$-orbitals in its second principal shell, limiting its maximum covalency to $4$
Boron has a higher electronegativity than aluminum
Aluminum has a lower ionization enthalpy
$\text{BF}_6^{3-}$ is destabilized by strong $p\pi-p\pi$ back bonding
questions.solution:
1. Boron has the valence electronic configuration $2s^2 2p^1$. In its second principal quantum shell ($n = 2$), there are only four atomic orbitals available for bonding: one $2s$ and three $2p$. Due to the complete absence of $d$-orbitals in Period 2, boron cannot expand its valence shell beyond an octet; its maximum coordination number (covalency) is strictly limited to $4$ (as in $[\text{BF}_4]^-$).
2. Aluminum has the valence configuration $3s^2 3p^1 3d^0$. It has low-lying vacant $3d$-orbitals, enabling it to expand its coordination number to $6$ to form octahedral complexes like $[\text{AlF}_6]^{3-}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] When anhydrous aluminum chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$) is dissolved in water, the major ionic species present in solution is:
questions.solution:
Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is a covalent dimer ($\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$) in the solid and vapor state.
When dissolved in water, the exceptionally high hydration enthalpy of the small, highly charged $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ion ($\Delta H_{\text{hyd}} \approx -4665\text{ kJ/mol}$) overcomes the covalent lattice and ionization energies.
It cleaves the chloride bridges and coordinates with six water molecules to form the octahedral hexaaqua complex cation:
$$\text{AlCl}_3(s) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}(aq) + 3\text{Cl}^-(aq)$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Carbon monoxide acts as a deadly poison in humans primarily because:
options: It binds to hemoglobin with an affinity roughly $200-300$ times greater than that of oxygen, forming carboxyhemoglobin
It oxidizes iron(II) in hemoglobin to iron(III)
It hydrolyzes in blood to form toxic formic acid
It rapidly reacts with carbon dioxide to deplete cellular oxygen
questions.solution:
Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) is a strong $\sigma$-donor and $\pi$-acceptor ligand.
It binds reversibly to the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ center in hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin:
$$\text{Hb} + \text{CO} \rightleftharpoons \text{HbCO}$$
The stability constant of carboxyhemoglobin is approximately $200-300\text{ times}$ greater than that of oxyhemoglobin ($\text{HbO}_2$).
This irreversible occupation blocks the binding sites for oxygen transport, causing cellular asphyxiation and death.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the oxides of carbon is FALSE?
options: $\text{CO}$ is an acidic oxide that readily dissolves in water to form carbonic acid
$\text{CO}_2$ is an acidic oxide that forms carbonic acid with water
$\text{CO}$ is a neutral oxide and acts as a powerful reducing agent at elevated temperatures
$\text{CO}_2$ has a linear geometry and a net dipole moment of zero
questions.solution:
1. Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$) is almost insoluble in water and is classified as a **neutral oxide** (it does not form an acid with water and does not react with aqueous bases at room temperature).
2. In contrast, carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) is an acidic oxide that dissolves in water to produce carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$).
Therefore, Statement A is false.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In pyrosilicates, how many oxygen atoms are shared per $[\text{SiO}_4]^{4-}$ tetrahedron?
questions.solution:
In pyrosilicates (also called sorosilicates or island silicates), two $[\text{SiO}_4]^{4-}$ tetrahedra are joined together by sharing exactly **one** corner oxygen atom between them.
Formula of pyrosilicate ion:
$$2[\text{SiO}_4]^{4-} - \text{O}^{2-} = [\text{Si}_2\text{O}_7]^{6-}$$
Examples include thortveitite ($\text{Sc}_2\text{Si}_2\text{O}_7$) and hemimorphite ($\text{Zn}_4(\text{OH})_2\text{Si}_2\text{O}_7 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Heating orthoboric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3$) above $370\text{ K}$ initially yields substance $X$, which on further red heat decomposes to form $Y$. $X$ and $Y$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
Thermal decomposition of orthoboric acid occurs in a stepwise manner:
1. Heated gently to $\approx 370-375\text{ K}$, it loses water to form metaboric acid ($\text{HBO}_2$):
$$\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta, 373\text{ K}} \text{HBO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. On heating $\text{HBO}_2$ to red heat, it loses more water to yield boric oxide / boric anhydride ($\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$):
$$2\text{HBO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{red heat}} \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Thus, $X$ is $\text{HBO}_2$ and $Y$ is $\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Find the total number of bridging hydrogen atoms present in one molecule of diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$).
questions.solution:
In diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$):
- There are $4$ terminal hydrogen atoms, each involved in a standard two-center two-electron ($2\text{c}-2\text{e}^-$) $\text{B}-\text{H}$ bond.
- There are $2$ bridge hydrogen atoms, each forming a three-center two-electron ($3\text{c}-2\text{e}^-$) bent $\text{B}-\text{H}-\text{B}$ bond.
Thus, the total number of bridging hydrogen atoms is $2.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the number of five-membered rings present in one molecule of Buckminsterfullerene ($\text{C}_{60}$).
questions.solution:
A $\text{C}_{60}$ fullerene molecule possesses a truncated icosahedral cage geometry.
According to Euler's polyhedral formula, the cage consists of:
- $20$ six-membered hexagonal rings
- $12$ five-membered pentagonal rings
Thus, the number of five-membered rings is $12.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] What is the oxidation state of lead in minium (red lead, $\text{Pb}_3\text{O}_4$) when treated as a mixed oxide $2\text{PbO} \cdot \text{PbO}_2$? Find the oxidation state of lead in the $\text{PbO}_2$ constituent.
questions.solution:
Red lead ($\text{Pb}_3\text{O}_4$) is a mixed oxide with stoichiometric composition $2\text{PbO} \cdot \text{PbO}_2$:
- In $\text{PbO}$ (lead(II) oxide), the oxidation state of lead is $+2$.
- In $\text{PbO}_2$ (lead(IV) oxide), the oxidation state of lead is $+4$.
Thus, the oxidation state of lead in the $\text{PbO}_2$ component is $4.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Calculate the total number of $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ bridge linkages present in a single borate anion unit of crystalline borax, $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$.
questions.solution:
The structural formula of borax is $\text{Na}_2[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4] \cdot 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
The central bicyclic ring of the polyanion $[\text{B}_4\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}$ consists of:
- Two $sp^2$ hybridized planar $\text{BO}_3$ units
- Two $sp^3$ hybridized tetrahedral $\text{BO}_4$ units
- Four $-\text{OH}$ groups bonded to the four boron atoms
- Five oxygen bridges ($\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ linkages), with four forming the outer cyclic framework and one cross-ring bridge linking the two tetrahedral borons.
Therefore, the number of $\text{B}-\text{O}-\text{B}$ linkages is $5.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Among the following halides: $\text{BF}_3, \text{BCl}_3, \text{AlCl}_3, \text{SiCl}_4, \text{CCl}_4, \text{SnCl}_2, \text{PbCl}_4$, how many act as Lewis acids under standard conditions?
questions.solution:
Assess Lewis acidity (ability to accept an electron pair):
1. $\text{BF}_3$: Incomplete octet (6 valence electrons) $\implies$ Lewis acid
2. $\text{BCl}_3$: Incomplete octet (6 valence electrons) $\implies$ Lewis acid
3. $\text{AlCl}_3$: Incomplete octet in monomer, forms adducts with donors $\implies$ Lewis acid
4. $\text{SiCl}_4$: Has vacant $3d$-orbitals, expands coordination sphere $\implies$ Lewis acid
5. $\text{CCl}_4$: Complete octet, no vacant $d$-orbitals, sterically hindered $\implies$ Not a Lewis acid
6. $\text{SnCl}_2$: Incomplete valence shell and vacant $d$-orbitals, forms $[\text{SnCl}_3]^-$ $\implies$ Lewis acid
7. $\text{PbCl}_4$: Accepts electron pairs into vacant $d$-orbitals (forms $[\text{PbCl}_6]^{2-}$) $\implies$ Lewis acid
Total count $= 6.0$ (all except $\text{CCl}_4$).
